title: A Simple Way To Build Trust And Likability With Your Entire Class
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin offers a simple daily practice for strengthening trust and likability, two teacher traits he identifies as the source of the leverage needed to manage any class. The strategy is to pause briefly after greeting students each day and voice genuine appreciation for the class as a group, sharing a few specific things the teacher values about them—distinct from praise, since it is framed as gratitude rather than evaluation. He provides a sample script and explains that the brief gesture creates a disarming softness in students, reminds them the teacher understands their effort, and triggers a reciprocal appreciation through the law of reciprocity. He notes the gesture doesn't require students to be perfect, since it speaks to who they are becoming as much as who they currently are, and closes by asking teachers to reflect on what genuinely makes them grateful for their class before delivering the message.
points: Trust and likability are identified as the source of the leverage a teacher needs to manage any class.
A brief daily expression of genuine appreciation for the class, distinct from praise, is the recommended strategy.
The gesture creates a disarming softness in students and triggers reciprocal goodwill through the law of reciprocity.
Students don't need to be perfect for the appreciation to be genuine—it can speak to who they are becoming.
Teachers are encouraged to reflect specifically on what they're grateful for in their class before delivering the message.
quotes: Together, they cause students to want to please you and behave for you. They give your consequences muscle and meaning.
The way it works is that after first greeting your students for the day, you're going to take a moment to express your appreciation for them.
It isn’t praise, per se. It’s more of an expression of your gratitude.
I’m happy to be your teacher, and I just wanted you to know that.
It causes a disarming softness, quietness, and ease in their bearing and attitude. It opens their awareness to all that you do for them.
You’re simultaneously fine-tuning, encouraging, and raising the stakes on your classroom tone and tenor while triggering the law of reciprocity that resides in every student.
